amendments.normalized_body: CleanFilter action (engine.rs:353-373) reduces microbe biomass by `intensity * 0.5` across all four guilds but does not route the removed biomass to dissolved organics or detritus. The element content (N and C) of the cleaned-off biomass silently vanishes. The budget guard masks this because `action:clean_filter` is listed as an open-system action in `tick_has_closed_system_nitrogen`. Fix: route the setback biomass to dissolved organic pools (same pattern as `route_live_biomass_to_dissolved_organics` in nitrogen_cycle.rs), and either remove `action:clean_filter` from the open-system exclusion list so the guard can verify conservation, or record an explicit export entry in the budget ledger.

The `test_total_n_helper_sums_all_pools` test (budget_tracking.rs:242-274) sums microbe biomass into a single `microbe_biomass_g` value and calls `manual_live_biomass_nitrogen_mg(microbe_biomass_g, ratio)` once, while `nitrogen_budget_components` computes N for each microbe guild individually. Because `live_biomass_nitrogen_mg` applies `max(0.0)` per guild and the organic_nitrogen formula `mass * 1000 * ratio / (1+ratio)` is linear, the results coincide only when all guilds are non-negative. The test happens to pass because the fixture values are all positive. A test with one guild at exactly 0.0 would still pass due to linearity, but the structural approach of testing the sum rather than each component separately means the test does not verify that each guild is individually accounted. Consider splitting the microbe budget assertion to check per-guild contributions, mirroring the actual component structure.

The `dissolved_feed_residue_g_total` bookkeeping field is decremented only by mineralization (nitrogen_cycle.rs:120-121) and water changes (water_change.rs:60), but not by `SiphonDetritus` (engine.rs:348-351) or `TrimPlants` (engine.rs:334-346). After siphoning, `dissolved_feed_residue_g_total` may exceed the sum of actual DOC+DON it shadows. While this field is excluded from the budget and is only used for filter clogging heuristics (nitrogen_cycle.rs:600), it can produce stale clogging signals post-siphon. Consider decrementing `dissolved_feed_residue_g_total` proportionally during siphoning, consistent with the other retained-fraction reductions already done for particulate and fine detritus.

In `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs`, make the closed-system budget guard depend on actual mass movement, not just the presence of an action label. Every queued action is recorded into the tick ledger (`step_one_hour`, lines 93-99), but several of the actions that are treated as open-system in `tick_has_closed_system_nitrogen`/`tick_has_closed_system_carbon` can be no-ops (`Feed { grams: 0.0 }`, `WaterChangePercent { percent: 0.0 }`, `SiphonDetritus { fraction: 0.0 }`, `CleanFilter { intensity: 0.0 }`, `AddShrimp { count: 0 }`, `RemoveShrimp { count: 0 }`; see `process_action`, lines 285-406). Because `tick_has_closed_system_nitrogen` only checks `entry.label` (`engine.rs`, lines 523-544), any such zero-effect action suppresses the conservation guard for that tick even though the tick is still closed. Use `BudgetEntry.delta` (or the original action parameters) so zero-delta/no-op actions do not disable the nitrogen/carbon balance check.
